title: Why Plague Doctors Wore Bird Masks
style: Stylized realistic 3D CGI animation still, high-end animated explainer look, Pixar-meets-realism, cinematic soft lighting, detailed skin, hair and fabric, expressive faces, shallow depth of field, no text, no letters, no gore, vertical 9:16 framing.

sections.name: Why Plague Doctors Wore Bird Masks

lines.prompt: A plague doctor in a long black waxed coat, wide-brimmed hat and white beaked bird mask walking down a foggy 17th-century cobbled street

lines: This is one of the creepiest outfits in history. The plague doctor.

lines.prompt: Close-up of the beaked mask on a wooden table, the beak opened to show dried flowers, herbs and lavender stuffed inside

lines: That long beak wasn't for show. It was stuffed with herbs, flowers and spices.

lines.prompt: Swirling green mist rising from a dirty medieval alley, frightened townspeople covering their noses

lines: Doctors believed plague spread through bad air, called miasma. The herbs were meant to filter it out.

lines.prompt: A plague doctor holding a long wooden cane, pointing at a patient from a distance without touching him, candlelit room

lines: They carried a cane, so they could examine patients without touching them.

lines.prompt: Close-up of a black rat on a ship's rope with a tiny flea glowing under soft light on its fur, harbour at night

lines: The real culprit was much smaller. Plague was mostly spread by fleas, carried on rats.

lines.prompt: The plague doctor at night taking off his mask under a lantern, revealing a tired ordinary young man's face

lines: The waxed coat may have helped a little, by keeping the fleas off. But the herbs did nothing.
